findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow has no typestate; any combination of status/is_validated/is_sent is representable including impossible states
findings.failure_mode: A caller can construct LedgerWorkflow { id: "x", status: "sent", is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } — a struct that claims neither validated nor sent while status reads 'sent', making invariant checks unreachable from the type
findings.fix: Replace struct with a typestate enum e.g. enum Ledger { New { id, validated: false } | Validated { id, validated: true } | Sent { id, validated: true, sent_at_ms } } with transitions gated on enum variants

findings.problem: status is String, allowing arbitrary values ("foo", "SENT", "", any future value) instead of a finite state set
findings.failure_mode: Downstream match/logic on status cannot be exhaustive; a misspelled or unexpected string silently bypasses state transitions, and serialized output can contain invalid state names
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `enum LedgerStatus { New, Validated, Sent }` and remove is_sent/is_validated bools

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans that can reach inconsistent combinations (e.g. validated=false, sent=true)
findings.failure_mode: The two booleans encode a 2x2 state machine independently of status; callers can set is_sent=true while is_validated=false, producing an invalid lifecycle that the type system cannot prevent
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum that owns the lifecycle transitions; variant-own the data each state needs

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is optional lifecycle data stored as a flat field, decoupled from the state machine — the Option can be None while is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None means the ledger thinks it is sent but has no timestamp, violating the invariant that sent entries carry a timestamp; the Option is independently mutable
findings.fix: Move sent_at_ms inside the typestate variant that owns it, e.g. Sent { id, sent_at_ms: u64 } — no Option, the timestamp is required by construction

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive used as a domain identifier; any string including empty or malformed values is accepted
findings.failure_mode: An empty-string or duplicate ID cannot be rejected at the type level; invalid IDs propagate through the system without smart-constructor validation
findings.fix: Define `pub struct LedgerId(String)` with a smart constructor `fn try_from(s: impl AsRef<str>) -> Result<LedgerId, ParseError>` that rejects empty/whitespace-only values

findings.problem: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors — callers construct LedgerWorkflow directly with String, bool, and Option fields
findings.failure_mode: No constructor enforces domain invariants; any caller can create a LedgerWorkflow in an illegal state (e.g. status="sent", is_sent=false, is_validated=true) bypassing all type-level guards
findings.fix: Remove all pub fields; provide private struct with `LedgerWorkflow::try_new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, Error>` smart constructor, and use typestate enum or at minimum an enum for status with sealed transitions

findings.problem: mark_sent sets status='sent' and is_sent=true without checking is_validated first, and accepts any prior state
findings.failure_mode: A ledger that was never validated can be directly marked as sent, violating the business invariant that only validated ledgers may be sent; the function has no Result type so the caller cannot detect that an invalid transition occurred
findings.fix: Change to `fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, TransitionError>` and require is_validated==true before allowing the transition, or use a typestate enum where mark_sent is only callable on the Validated variant

findings.problem: No benchmarks, profiler data, or allocation evidence exist for the crate; mark_sent performs a heap allocation via "sent".to_string() on every call
findings.failure_mode: The repeated `.to_string()` allocation in a hot path is unmeasured and unbounded; if this is called in a tight loop it causes unnecessary heap allocations that could be replaced with a &'static str or enum variant
findings.fix: Replace `item.status = "sent".to_string()` with a static string `"sent"` or better an enum variant; add a benchmark demonstrating the allocation profile

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or LedgerWorkflow operations
no profiler data showing allocation hot paths
no command evidence that cargo fmt/check/clippy/test were run
no allocation budget or try_reserve evidence for any hot path
residual_risk: The struct encodes no invariants — any combination of fields is legal, making the typestate machine, status enum, bool lifecycle, Option data, parse boundary, and mark_sent guard all violated simultaneously. This is a fundamental architectural failure: the domain model cannot represent valid states. Without typestate enum replacement, no amount of linting or testing can guarantee correctness.
